- **M5** (2026-09-22T17:41:52.812Z) — Version bumps: the version string appears SIX times per file, not once. packages/engine/package.json carries `version` plus five sofar-core optional deps (sofar-core-darwin-arm64, -darwin-x64, -linux-x64, -linux-arm64, -win32-x64) pinned to the same string, and package-lock.json repeats all six. Setting only `version` ships a package whose five core-binary pins resolve the PREVIOUS release — a stale binary on whichever platform nobody tests locally (win32-x64, or a linux arch). So bump by replacing the version string GLOBALLY in both files, and self-check before committing: the result parses as JSON, ZERO occurrences of the old string remain anywhere, the engine version equals the new one, and exactly five sofar-core deps are pinned to it — a count, never an eyeball. Do not use `npm install --package-lock-only` to do it: it can reach the network, against the zero-egress invariant (SPEC §Architectural invariants). (3) packaging/npm/sofar-core-*/package.json — the five platform packages each carry their OWN `version`, and packaging.test.ts asserts each equals the engine manifest's, so missing them fails the suite. Also learned: the five sofar-core-<platform> packages have NEVER been published (npm view → 404 at any version), so an install resolves none of them and install.mjs keeps the JavaScript shim by design — "a missing binary is no core, never a broken install". Pinning them at a new version is therefore safe, and publishing the native core is a separate decision.
And: a release branch in a git worktree must NOT share node_modules with the main checkout by symlink. npm's workspace links inside it point at the MAIN tree, so `require('sofar.sh/package.json')` returns main's version and the packaging test fails with the old string. Give the worktree its own node_modules whose `sofar.sh` and `@sofar/schema` links point INTO the worktree.
